questions.question: Differentiate between primary and secondary lymphoid organs .
questions.solution_html:
• (Primary lymphoid organ-(2 marks),Secondary lymphoid organ-(2marks))
  • Primary lymphoid organs are where lymphocytes mature, while secondary lymphoid organs are
  • where they are activated.Primary lymphoid organs include the bone marrow (B cell maturation) and
  • the thymus (T cell maturation). Secondary lymphoid organs, such as the spleen, lymph nodes
  • tonsils, and Peyer's patches, are sites where mature lymphocytes encounter antigens and mount
  • immune responses.
questions.final_answer: immune responses

questions.question: Describe the principle and procedure of capsule staining.
questions.solution_html:
• (Principle-(2Marks),Procedur-(2 Marks))
  • Capsule staining is a differential staining method that uses acidic and basic dyes to stain the
  • background and cell, leaving the capsule unstained as a clear halo.The procedure involves mixing
  • bacteria with an acidic stain (e.g., Congo red or nigrosin) and spreading it thinly on a slide. The
  • smear is air-dried (not heat-fixed to prevent capsule shrinkage/destruction) and then counterstained
  • with a basic dye (e.g., crystal violet or safranin) to stain the cell body. The resulting slide shows
  • stained cells surrounded by a clear, unstained capsule against a dark background.
questions.final_answer: stained cells surrounded by a clear, unstained capsule against a dark background
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write an essay on cells of the immune system.
questions.solution_html:
• ( B cell-(2 Marks),T Cells-(1 Marks),NK Cells-(1 Marks))
  • The immune system comprises a diverse array of specialized cells that work together to defend the
  • body against pathogens and disease.Lymphocytes (T cells, B cells, NK cells): Responsible for
  • specific recognition of antigens and adaptive immunity. B cells produce antibodies, while T cells
  • mediate cellular responses.Phagocytes (Macrophages, Neutrophils): Engulf and destroy
  • pathogens and cellular debris.Antigen-Presenting Cells (Dendritic cells
  • Macrophages): Process antigens and present them to T cells to initiate an immune
  • response.Granulocytes (Mast cells, Eosinophils, Basophils): Contain granules with chemicals
  • that mediate inflammation and allergic reactions.
questions.final_answer: that mediate inflammation and allergic reactions
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Illustrate the working principle of a SEM with a neat labelled diagram.
questions.solution_html:
• (PRINCIPLE-(2 Marks),Diagrammatic representation-(2Marks))
  • A Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) produces high-resolution images of a sample's surface by
  • scanning it with a focused beam of electrons.Principle: The electron beam interacts with the atoms
  • in the sample, producing various signals like secondary electrons (used for imaging the topography)
  • and backscattered electrons.Procedure: The signals are detected by specialized detectors, and an
  • image is
  • built up pixel by pixel, showing the surface morphology and composition. A neat, labeled diagram
  • would typically show the electron source, electromagnetic lenses, scanning coils, sample chamber
  • detectors, and display screen.
questions.final_answer: detectors, and display screen
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Illustrate the working principle of a SEM with a neat labelled diagram.
questions.solution_html:
• (PRINCIPLE-(2 Marks),Diagrammatic representation-(2Marks))
  • A Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) produces high-resolution images of a sample's surface by
  • scanning it with a focused beam of electrons.Principle: The electron beam interacts with the atoms
  • in the sample, producing various signals like secondary electrons (used for imaging the topography)
  • and backscattered electrons.Procedure: The signals are detected by specialized detectors, and an
  • image is
  • built up pixel by pixel, showing the surface morphology and composition. A neat, labeled diagram
  • would typically show the electron source, electromagnetic lenses, scanning coils, sample chamber
  • detectors, and display screen.
